crest_depth_m.datum: below MSL (design minimum, per the original Skelly Engineering plan-view drawing's own annotation 'TOP OF BAG MIN DEPTH -6' MSL' at both arm tips; 6 ft = 1.83 m). Card's other cited sources give two additional, conflicting as-surveyed/as-reported figures on different datums: -0.9 m MLLW (R4) and ~2.4 m/8 ft at zero tide (R7, Surfrider-sourced, quoted by a Surfline commenter) - not resolved here, likely partly a datum (MSL vs MLLW vs 'zero tide') difference.

distance_offshore_m.measured_from: shoreline (approximate; card's R1 states only '~100 yards/100 m off the beach', not a precise engineering survey; ~100 yards = 91.4 m)

orientation_notes: The reinforced central 'spine' block (where the two arms of bags converge) is the most-offshore point of the structure and faces the 'WAVE DIRECTION' arrow drawn on the Skelly Engineering plan view, i.e. the apex points seaward into the incident swell, consistent with the card's design narrative ('arms at roughly 45 degrees to the predominant swell, meant to focus and peel incoming waves'). The drawing's own 45-degree angle annotation (measured from a vertical reference line to one arm) and this file's pixel-geometry check (~92 degrees between the two arms, i.e. ~46 degrees each side of the wave-direction axis) agree closely. The two arms are markedly ASYMMETRIC: ~44 m from spine to one tip, ~33 m to the other (a ~25% difference) - a refinement on Gemini's near-symmetric 9-vertex polygon. No compass bearing for the wave-direction axis, and no indication of which arm points which alongshore (e.g. north vs south) direction, could be determined from the design drawing itself (no north arrow). Gemini's specific '260-280 deg, W-WNW' bearing is plausible for a Santa Monica Bay/El Segundo south-/west-facing beach but is not confirmed in any source in our card or found in this pass.
materials: ~200 sand-filled geotextile (described as polyester/black polypropylene) bags total, built in two phases: 110 bags fall 2000 (this drawing's exact bag count) + ~90 more bags spring 2001; individual bags ~14 tons (R4) or ~14,000 lb (R7) - sources disagree ~2x; bag footprint 3 m x 1.2 m per the Raised Water Research bag-size diagram (R4) [R1][R2][R4][R7].

Crest depth (1.8 m) is very close to the '-6 ft MSL' (1.83 m) design-minimum-depth label we found directly on the original Skelly drawing (R4) - though Gemini did not cite that drawing (it cites Henriquez/Surfrider/Borrero-Nelsen instead, none of which we could confirm state this figure), this specific number checks out against a primary source we located.
Distance offshore (95 m) falls within our own card's approximate '~100 yards/100 m' range (R1) - reasonable agreement.

Gemini's envelope is 30-45% smaller in both dimensions than what the primary design source shows; none of Gemini's three cited sources (Henriquez 2005 thesis, Surfrider Decommissioning Assessment 2008, Borrero & Nelsen 2003) were found by us to state a numeric 40x20 m footprint anywhere - the task brief's own suspicion is confirmed.

open_issues: This file's Skelly-drawing-based measurements (R4) describe the Phase I design only (110 bags + up to 30 'optional' bags = up to 140), matching the fall-2000 as-built count exactly. No plan-view drawing was found anywhere in our references for the spring-2001 Phase II addition (~90 more bags, bringing the total to ~200 built) - the FINAL as-built footprint (2001-2008) may have been somewhat larger than reported here, by an unknown amount.

The arm cross-section width (4 m) and spine-block size (8x6 m) used to turn the drawing's bag-chain centrelines into a closed polygon are this file's own estimate (from the bag-size diagram and visual inspection), not a published figure - area_m2 (324.1) should be read as order-of-magnitude only, not a precise footprint.

No compass bearing or north arrow appears on the Skelly drawing; this file's alongshore (x) axis direction is an arbitrary, stated-but-unverified convention (same limitation flagged in the parallel cables-reef-wa.md file for that reef).

The card's own two pre-existing crest-depth figures (-0.9 m MLLW per R4's text vs ~2.4 m/8 ft at zero tide per R7) remain unresolved; this file's new '-6 ft MSL' (1.83 m) reading from the drawing itself is a third data point, close to but not identical to either, plausibly a datum (MSL vs MLLW vs 'zero tide') difference rather than a genuine conflict - not resolved here.

image26.png's single '200 m' scale bar was shown (via the Narrowneck cross-check) not to transfer reliably across the graphic's 4 photo panels; its Pratte's-specific reading (~68.5x34.3 m) is reported for completeness in the derivation table only and is excluded from this file's headline/confidence-bearing numbers.

All pixel measurements come from a low-resolution (308x385 px) scanned engineering drawing; scale-bar tick-mark reading, bag-corner anti-aliasing, and line thickness contribute an estimated +/-10% uncertainty to every length/width/area figure derived from it.
